questions.question: Ben pours out 36 identical square tiles and pushes them together on his desk with no gaps. He makes rows that all hold the same number of tiles, and he wants the number of rows to match the number of tiles in each row. How many tiles are in each row?
questions.explain: A square array needs the same number of rows as tiles in each row, and 6 × 6 = 36, so each row holds 6. The trap is treating squaring as doubling: 18 and 18 make 36, but 18 rows of 18 would need far more tiles.

questions.question: A patio is covered with 64 identical square stones packed with no gaps. There are 8 rows, and each row holds exactly 8 stones, with none left over. Why is 64 called a perfect square?
options: Because 64 is an even number with no leftovers
Because 8 rows of 8 fill the square exactly
Because 64 sits close to the round number 60
Because 8 squared means 8 and 8, which is 16
questions.explain: A number is a perfect square when its items fill a complete n × n array, and here 8 × 8 = 64. Watch out: 8 squared means 8 × 8 = 64, not 8 + 8 = 16.

questions.question: A tray holds 100 identical square chocolates packed edge to edge with no gaps: there are 10 rows, and each row holds 10 chocolates. Which reason best shows that 100 is a perfect square?
options: 100 is a round number that ends in two zeros
100 is double 50, and doubling makes squares
100 fills a 10 by 10 square with none left
100 is the biggest number on a hundred chart
questions.explain: 100 is a perfect square because 10 × 10 = 100 fills a 10 by 10 array, not because it looks round. Plenty of round numbers, like 20 or 50, cannot make a square array at all.

questions.question: A Grade 7 class has 121 identical square carpet tiles. They want to push all 121 tiles together into one big square on the floor, with the same number of rows as tiles in each row and none left over. Is that possible?
options: No, because only round counts like 120 work
No, because 11 squared means 11 and 11, or 22
Yes, because 12 rows of 12 use every tile
Yes, because 11 rows of 11 use every tile
questions.explain: 121 tiles make an 11 by 11 square, since 11 × 11 = 121, so it is a perfect square. A 12 by 12 square would need 144 tiles, and round counts like 120 do not form squares.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is a perfect square?
questions.explain: 144 is a perfect square because 12 × 12 = 144 makes a 12 by 12 array. The numbers 10 and 20 only look tidy, and 24 is double 12 rather than 12 times itself.

questions.question: Mei arranges counters on her desk into a square array with 9 counters in every row and 9 rows in total. How many counters does she use altogether?
questions.explain: A 9 by 9 array holds 9 × 9 = 81 counters, so 81 is a perfect square. Doubling 9 gives 18, which would only fill two rows.

questions.question: Which set contains only perfect squares?
questions.explain: 16 = 4 × 4, 25 = 5 × 5 and 36 = 6 × 6, so each one makes a square array. Round numbers such as 10, 20, 30 and doubles such as 6, 8, 10 do not.

questions.question: How many perfect squares are there from 100 to 144, counting both ends?
questions.explain: In that range the perfect squares are 10 × 10, 11 × 11 and 12 × 12, so there are 3. Numbers like 110 or 140 look round but cannot form an equal-sided array.

questions.question: Priya has 120 square patio stones. She wants to build the biggest possible square array in her yard, with the same number of rows as stones in each row, and store whatever is left. What happens?
options: 10 by 10, with 20 stones left to store
12 by 12, with no stones left to store
None left over, since 120 is a square
questions.explain: The biggest square that fits inside 120 is 10 × 10 = 100, so 20 stones are left over; 11 × 11 = 121 already needs one stone too many. Being a round number does not make 120 a perfect square.

questions.question: A community garden bed holds 144 seedlings arranged in a square array. The next bed is also a square array, but each row has 3 fewer seedlings than a row in the first bed. How many seedlings fit in the second bed?
questions.explain: 144 seedlings means 12 rows of 12, so 3 fewer in each row gives 9 × 9 = 81. Taking 3 off the total to get 141 changes the wrong number, because the 3 comes off each row.

questions.question: Liam writes 6² = 12 and says that 12 must be a perfect square. What went wrong?
options: Nothing, since 12 is a round, even number
12 works, since 12 tiles make 3 rows of 4
questions.explain: 6² means a 6 by 6 array, so 6 × 6 = 36; squaring is never doubling. A perfect square also needs equal sides, so a 3 by 4 rectangle does not count.

questions.question: Sofia is tiling a square backsplash that is 11 tiles across and 11 tiles down, with no gaps. Each square tile costs $3. What is the total cost of the tiles?
questions.explain: The square array holds 11 × 11 = 121 tiles, and 121 × 3 = 363 dollars. Rounding 121 down to 120 or doubling 11 to get 22 both change the size of the square.
